newsitem.title: MEXICO: World tequila supplies at risk, say producers.
newsitem.headline: World tequila supplies at risk, say producers.

text.p: Margarita drinkers around the world may have to go without as tequila producers said on Monday that a bank debtors' blockade of installations threatened world supplies.
"There is a risk of supplies running out...both at home and abroad," said Jorge Camacho Ornelas, vice president of the Tequila Producers Chamber.

A branch of the "El Barzon" debtors' organization representing growers of agave cactus began their blockade of the town of Tequila on September 19. Trucks carrying agave and sugar have neither entered nor left the town since then.
The growers are protesting the low price they receive for agave, an essential ingredient in making tequila.
The 11 installations blockaded account for 70 percent of tequilla exports, and some 750,000 U.S. gallons of production have been lost since the blockade began, the tequilla producers' grouo said.
